findings.claim_reviewed: Generosity, learning, pride and Janaka’s attributed cosmic self-claim versus Nārada’s devotion argument.
findings.assessment: 65.10 is Nārada’s question about growing wealth;65.12 is his praise of Gaṇeśa’s devotional generosity;65.13–14 is Janaka’s own claim. Patch preserves the speaker distinctions and does not certify the king as cosmic creator.

findings.claim_reviewed: Nārada departure and deity’s repulsive old-Brahmin test manifestation.
findings.assessment: Narrator65.19 explicitly identifies Gajānana testing royal devotion; Janaka separately wonders whether the guest is God65.26–27. Blood, flies, missing teeth, stumbling/fainting and gate admission are directly supported.

findings.claim_reviewed: The guest first asks food until satisfied and conditionally promises hundred-sacrifice merit; immense servings fail.
findings.assessment: 65.29–30 is the guest’s food/satisfaction request to Janaka, not a personal liberation request by the poor couple. One-mouthful portions and prepared food sufficient for ten thousand65.32–34 are supported. Conditional merit is not recorded as earned.

findings.claim_reviewed: Unquenched appetite exhausts city/village grain; the visitor enters Virocanā and Triśiras’s poor home.
findings.assessment: 65.36–37 presents conjectures by onlookers, not proof of a Rākṣasa identity.65.38–43 explicitly keeps the guest unsatisfied and Janaka downcast.65.44 prints virocanātriśirasor ... dvijayor;66.12 names Virocanā as giver and66.16/22 names Triśiras as embraced devotee. No identification with unrelated epic/asura actors is made.

findings.claim_reviewed: Virocanā and Triśiras are a devoted married pair rather than two unrelated beggars.
findings.assessment: 66.7 speaker label dam-patī and66.19 dam-patī link the previously named pair. Their bare-earth/sky-cover austerity, unasked food, water rites and exclusive image worship are supported. The tiny devotional gift versus ostentation teaching66.9 is preserved.

findings.claim_reviewed: The marital assertion currently cites only66.1–9, where the named pair is contextual.
findings.assessment: The relationship is supported in context, but the stored evidence span should include the actual named-pair attestation65.44 to make the actor allocation independently traceable. This is a locator-strengthening correction, not a rejected spouse relationship.
findings.proposed_action: Add gup5-e-033 alongside gup5-e-034; optionally gup5-e-036 supplies the second explicit couple address.

findings.claim_reviewed: Triśiras is typed SAGE although the reviewed body calls him a Brahmin and devotee.
findings.assessment: 65.44 supplies dvija, and66.22 bhaktaṃ triśirasaṃ. These bodies contain no sage epithet establishing this entity type. This review cannot prove that no other passage calls him a sage; it only checks the evidence assigned to this source-local record.
findings.proposed_action: Use DEVOTEE (or PERSON) for this local entity, unless an independently read passage explicitly establishes SAGE; preserve ID and name.

findings.claim_reviewed: One leftover morning-worship dūrvā and imagined food satisfy the guest.
findings.assessment: 66.11 asks the single sprout;66.12 explicitly makes Virocanā the giver.66.13–14 lists rice, pāyasa, cooked foods, accompaniments and lickable/suckable foods imagined upon it. The guest eats it; stomach-fire ceases and complete satisfaction follows. The patch correctly keeps imagined dishes distinct from physical provisions. Digital66.15 is printed5 between14 and16; body continuity is clear, with no omitted unit inferred.

findings.claim_reviewed: Four-armed reveal holding lotus, axe, rosary and tusk.
findings.assessment: Four arms, trunk, lotus eyes and four listed hand objects are explicit. No extra mount, parentage or weapon gift is inferred.

findings.claim_reviewed: The couple’s final request is devotion in whatever birth OR liberation; deity explicitly assents and vanishes.
findings.assessment: 66.20 requests firm devotion wherever born;66.21 supplies muktiḥ vā and no other wish;66.22 has tathā assent, another embrace of Triśiras and disappearance. Patch preserves the alternatives and does not select one, add wealth, or invent a later death/vehicle. The bounded feeding-test ending is present; COMPLETE for this declared scene is supported, subject to small role/evidence corrections.

findings.claim_reviewed: Kauṇḍinya explains his offering and the history’s hearing/telling benefits.
findings.assessment: Devotional hearing/telling, sons/wealth/enjoyment, devotion and specifically desireless liberation are source-attributed conditions, not a narrated new grant to Virocanā/Triśiras.

findings.claim_reviewed: Aśrayā’s renewed doubt leads to a distinct exact-equal-weight gold request to Indra.
findings.assessment: The Gaṇas resume the enclosing narration, Kauṇḍinya knows Aśrayā’s doubt and commands one sprout and gold neither less nor more; she follows her husband’s word. This is separate from the poor couple’s final wish.

findings.claim_reviewed: 67.26 says three worlds failed to equal one sprout;67.40 says they became equal by the leaf on a scale.
findings.assessment: Both readings are directly present:67.26 trilokyam api nālabhat versus67.40 ... abhavat samam. No lexical or temporal reconciliation can be established from this one witness. Keeping the weighing story PARTIAL and conflict OPEN is appropriate.
findings.proposed_action: Retain both descriptors and require independent edition/Sanskrit collation; no equality result should overwrite the trial.

findings.claim_reviewed: The actual later abode transfer concerns Kauṇḍinya/Aśrayā, not Virocanā/Triśiras.
findings.assessment: 67.32–37 names Aśrayā and husband Kauṇḍinya; their continuous morning/evening worship precedes67.38–39 svadhāma pratyapādayat. Patch correctly assigns the actual joint transport to this enclosing couple, while66 only assents to the other couple’s requested alternatives.
